articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after 18 months on the job, the White House said Monday, in the latest departure of a top military leader during the Trump administration.
articles.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down, White House says

articles.author: Hugo Rikard-Bell
articles.description: While the high-profile shooting at Utah Valley University had only one homicide victim, Kirk's assassination was witnessed by thousands in person and even more as video spread online.
articles.title: Nearly 200 witnesses to Charlie Kirk shooting apply for victims' benefits in Utah

articles.author: Hansi Lo Wang
articles.description: After the Census Bureau issued a report tied to a Trump-aligned think tank, the bureau's parent agency cut language banning political interference from its scientific integrity policy, NPR learned.
articles.title: Trump officials cut political interference ban after unusual Census Bureau report

articles.author: Durrie Bouscaren
articles.description: The highly regarded FEWS NET network stopped posting data on Afghanistan, Somalia and Yemen -- then says it will start posting again in September. What's the reason for this back-and-forth?
articles.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened

articles.author: Bobby Allyn
articles.description: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.
articles.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades

articles.author: Alina Selyukh
articles.description: Federal regulators and 22 states allege that the tech giant made billions by manipulating how much brands and sellers paid for ads on its platform.
articles.title: The U.S. sues Amazon again

articles.description: Former Congressman George Santos has been banned from the prediction market site Kalshi for life. The betting site announced several enforcement actions against suspected insider traders.
articles.title: Former Congressman George Santos has been banned from Kalshi for life

articles.author: Tonya Mosley
articles.description: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.
articles.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The soccer star is ending 21 years of Argentine national-team duty but will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in U.S. Major League Soccer.
articles.title: Lionel Messi says he's retiring from playing internationally for Argentina

articles.author: Mamita Bhandari
articles.description: A group of the country's private sector power producers says Nepali authorities lost crucial time in rescuing hundreds of people trapped in hydropower tunnels.
articles.title: Nepal's hesitance to accept foreign help for flood relief comes under scrutiny

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Follow updates live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

43 Australians still missing, with concerns growing ‘every day, every hour’ that goes by, Wong says
The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, says there are still 43 Australian missing after the flooding in Nepal, saying the government holds grave concerns for their safety that only gets worse as the days go by.
This is such a distressing time and I know this is so difficult for the family and friends of those 43 Australians.
Every day, every hour, only increases our concern for those who have not been found and remain missing, and that is many Australians. … You can imagine how many families and friends are traumatised as a consequence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: PM shuts down questions of China ‘bullying’ on eve of Pacific forum; Victorian police officer charged after allegedly hitting teen with baton

articles.author: Sam Jones in Madrid
articles.description:
City council emphasises economic case for Madring amid local outrage over disruption and environmental impact
Opponents of Madrid’s newly constructed Formula One circuit have accused the regional authorities of putting profit before people’s wellbeing after tests for the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the track later this month yielded noise levels that were almost twice the legal decibel limit.
The regional government of Madrid and the city council are hoping that the 5.4km-long (3.3 miles) Madring circuit – which has been built in the north-east of the Spanish capital at a cost of €83m (£71m) – will attract visitors, boost the local economy and put the city firmly on the motor racing map. The Madring bills itself as “a perfectly connected circuit: just 20 minutes from the city centre”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Madrid residents brace for noise and disruption from new F1 circuit

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Chancellor says he wants everyone from apprentices to senior economists to take part in brainstorming exercise
John Healey has asked junior Treasury staff – including IT workers and apprentices – to send him ideas for his October budget, saying he will listen to all suggestions regardless of grade or profession.
The chancellor’s unorthodox approach comes as he faces a tricky autumn with expected inflation rises, sluggish growth and potential cuts from other departments to fund extra defence spending.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: John Healey invites October budget ideas from Treasury staff of all levels

articles.author: Hilary Osborne
articles.description:
Exclusive: FCA pressures firms to do more to sort 760,000 accounts as watchdog urges families to use free tracking service
Child trust fund providers are being put under the spotlight to check they are treating savers fairly and doing all they can to reunite young people with lost accounts.
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said about 760,000 accounts worth an average of £2,000 were yet to be claimed – more than £1.5bn in total – as it launched a review of the market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Child trust fund firms face review over efforts to find who owns £1.5bn worth of pots

articles.author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
articles.description:
A yes to membership would have given Brussels a boost but Icelanders have not voted to isolate themselves 
Iceland’s 52.8% to 47.2% vote against reopening EU accession talks is, undeniably, a blow for Brussels. But claiming it as a Brexit-style victory for “national sovereignty” or evidence of broad rejection of the EU misrepresents the reality of the island’s relationship with the bloc.
For the EU, Iceland was a dream candidate: small, stable, prosperous and strategically located in an increasingly contested Arctic. Eager as it is to wield more geopolitical clout and revive flagging momentum around enlargement, a vote in favour would have given Brussels a very welcome boost.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iceland’s close ties with EU mean no vote is not a Brexit-style rejection

articles.author: Penry Buckley
articles.description:
Sally Dowling tells budget estimates that Michael Daley called to tell her he was appointing a senior counsel and ‘raised quite a number of names’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The top prosecutor in NSW says she discussed a list of barristers to lead an independent review into controversial findings against her office with the state’s attorney general, before he appointed someone she had known “professionally and socially” for nearly 30 years.
Last month, a state parliamentary committee voted 4-3 to find that the New South Wales director of public prosecutions (DPP), Sally Dowling SC, had given false evidence about the pitching of a story about an Indigenous child performing an acknowledgement of country at a sentencing hearing to radio station 2GB.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW top prosecutor Sally Dowling and state attorney general discussed which barristers could review her office, estimates hears

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
articles.description:
Critically endangered New Zealand bird enjoys record breeding season triggered by mass fruiting of native tree, pushing its numbers to 325
The population of the world’s heaviest parrot, the kākāpō, has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years, after a record breeding season triggered by the mass fruiting of a native New Zealand tree.
Ninety chicks were officially added to the population of the critically endangered birds on 1 September, pushing the total to 325 – a record high since recovery efforts began.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kākāpō rising: 90 chicks swell population of the world’s heaviest parrot

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

US supreme court allows Trump to keep building $400m White House ballroom


Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Chris Hippensteel
We’re watching today as Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, and Kevin Warsh, the chair of the Federal Reserve, deliver their opening remarks at the G20 meetings in Asheville, North Carolina.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s ballroom construction can resume at White House, supreme court rules – as it happened

articles.author: Dani Anguiano and Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
A Las Vegas jury on Monday found Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty in the 1996 murder of the hip-hop icon

Jury finds Duane Davis guilty of murder of Tupac Shakur

Thirty years after the killing of Tupac Shakur, conspiracy theories and rumors about the perpetrator’s identity, one man has now been held criminally responsible for the rap icon’s death.
A Las Vegas jury convicted Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a 63-year-old former South Side Compton Crips gang leader, of murder for his role in the drive-by shooting. During the two-week long trial, prosecutors argued Davis was the “on-the-ground, on-site commander of the effort to kill Tupac” and had sought revenge after the musician was involved in a fight with his nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thirty years of waiting, a memoir and a trial: conviction in Tupac Shakur killing brings closure

articles.author: Joanna Walters
articles.description:
Phantom Ranch, set up by Teddy Roosevelt, has welcomed exhausted hikers to its famed cabins for over a century

Two dead and nearly 80 rescued after Grand Canyon flash flood

Phantom Ranch has been a solitary refuge visited by some of the most famous names of history. More typically, it’s been a beacon for the half-collapsed, exhausted and overheated hikers trudging down the Grand Canyon for more than a century.
The sole lodge at the very bottom of the Grand Canyon, the cabins long had a near mythical reputation. Located along the Bright Angel Creek, which tumbles into the mighty Colorado River at the base of the canyon, they served as a reminder of the long history of one of America’s most spectacular but savage environments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Remote Grand Canyon lodge hit by deadly flash flood boasts fabled history

articles.author: Gabrielle Canon
articles.description:
Flash flooding in Arizona tourist destination was likely triggered by compounding climate factors, such as drought and warming in Pacific Ocean

Remote Grand Canyon lodge hit by deadly flash flood boasts fabled history

A deadly flash flood in the Grand Canyon over the weekend was likely driven by a confluence of climate factors, including drought, wildfire scarring and warming temperatures in the Pacific Ocean that can supercharge storms.
At least two people have died, nearly 80 people were rescued and one remained unaccounted for after a surge of water and debris swept through the immensely popular tourist destination on Saturday, fueled by torrents of rain that hit the national park’s Bright Angel Creek area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How intense rains in the Grand Canyon turned into a deadly disaster

articles.author: Gabrielle Canon and agencies
articles.description:
Officials say one person still unaccounted for as forecast heavy rain and thunderstorms threaten further flooding
A second death was confirmed by National Park Service officials on Monday after a flash flood sent a surge of water and debris through an area of the Grand Canyon over the weekend.
Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter during the deluge, which consumed trails and infrastructure. Nearly 80 people were rescued and one person is still unaccounted for, as more heavy rain and thunderstorms in the forecasts threaten additional debris flows, flash floods or rock falls, the NPS said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two people dead and nearly 80 rescued after Grand Canyon flash flood

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Alleged offenders at large after man in his early 20s fatally shot in early hours of Tuesday

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man in his early 20s has been fatally shot in an alleged home invasion in Sydney’s south-west that police believe was a “targeted attack”. A homicide investigation is under way, with the alleged offenders still at large.
Acting Supt Gretchin Atkins said the man, who was yet to be formally identified, was at his Glen Alpine home with his family in the early hours of Tuesday morning when multiple individuals allegedly broke in.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sydney home invasion during which man shot and killed a ‘targeted attack’, police believe

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
‘Opera House of the west’ still slated to open to the public as scheduled on 7 November, NSW arts minister says

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An investigation is under way into allegations of misconduct involving senior executives at the soon-to-be-opened Powerhouse Parramatta.
The $915m museum in western Sydney, billed as one of the world’s most significant new museum projects, is set to open in November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Investigation into Powerhouse Parramatta museum under way as stop-gap leader steps in

articles.author: Damien Gayle Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Report calls for legally binding targets to cut microplastic pollution as soil ‘is a complex living ecosystem’
The accumulation of microplastics in soil presents an emerging threat to the UK’s food security, according to scientists, MPs and campaigners who have called for legally binding targets to cut microplastic pollution.
UK agricultural soils have been identified as among the most contaminated by microplastics in Europe, often as a result of repeated applications of sludge from water treatment works as fertiliser, according to a report published by the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) on microplastics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rising microplastics in soil a threat to UK food security, MPs and campaigners say

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Premium of nearly 10% paid by housebuyers comparable with cost of a cheaper private school over seven years
A house near a top state secondary school costs an extra £40,000 on average, according to research that reveals education premiums that rank alongside some private school fees.
The average property in a postcode district that includes a top 50 state secondary commands a price tag of £415,791, compared with £375,217 across the wider local authority areas in which those schools are located, a UK-wide analysis by the estate agent Yopa found.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK houses near top state secondary schools cost £40,000 more, research reveals

articles.author: Helena Horton and Harry Cockburn
articles.description:
From a darling of the Tory right to a moderate former army officer, we profile the key players

Andrew Griffith and Tom Tugendhat join Badenoch’s top team in Tory reshuffle

Kemi Badenoch has kicked off the return to parliament with a reshuffle of her top team in order to take on Andy Burnham and Reform UK. She has made sweeping changes to the shadow cabinet and ruthlessly axed her shadow chancellor. Here is a run-down of the new characters sitting across from Labour on the opposition frontbench.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team?

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
TCG Isin expected to play vital role in locating Filo Jet’s voyage data recorder 514 metres below surface
A deep-sea search and rescue vessel is on its way to Cyprus as Turkey joins efforts to retrieve the 20 people still missing after a passenger ferry capsized off the island’s northern coast.
The TCG Isin will join the vast operation to find survivors after the high-speed ferry sank on Sunday barely four nautical miles outside the port town of Kyrenia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Turkish deep-sea search vessel joins efforts to retrieve 20 still missing after Cyprus ferry disaster

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now); Yohannes Lowe, Martin Belam and Adam Fulton (earlier)
articles.description:
Iran responded to an assault on its Larak Island by targeting US bases in Jordan

Trump threatens further action as US and Iran exchange fire in new flare-up

Coinciding with this week’s G20 meeting, the EU has issued a statement saying it will work with the US and other allied countries to maintain economic pressure against Iran.
“The ‌EU welcomes efforts at ensuring that Iran ceases its destabilising activities and engages in peace negotiations with good ‌faith, also through additional economic pressure, including through ​the US-led Operation Economic Outcast,” it said in reference to the pressure strategy the White House describes as “an unprecedented campaign to sever every remaining economic lifeline sustaining” the Islamic republic.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says US will ‘hit Iran hard’ as hostilities resume – as it happened

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Washington says it acted after observing Iran was planning to deploy fresh mines in strait of Hormuz
The US and Iran have exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with missiles and drones fired at Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz, and Iran targeting US military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates in response.
The US president, Donald Trump, on Monday threatened further action. The US is to trying to prise open Tehran’s grip on shipping going through the strait, which before the war accounted for a fifth of the world’s seaborne energy supply. Washington claimed that Iranian control over the waterway had been loosened by repeated US attacks on Iranian missile launchers and radars.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump threatens further action as US and Iran exchange fire in new flare-up

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Frank Furedi announces resignation from MCC Brussels after organisation’s staff ‘not paid in July or August’
The head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite Brussels thinktank has quit, citing unpaid wages since the change of government in Hungary.
The sociology professor Frank Furedi said he was resigning as the executive director of MCC Brussels with “immediate effect” on Monday over “persistent failure to provide the contractually agreed funds”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite thinktank quits over unpaid wages

articles.author: Cait Kelly in Kathmandu and William Christou
articles.description:
Workers thought to be stuck in underground areas at 11 sites after last week’s devastating flash floods
Rescue teams are working to reach more than 900 missing hydropower workers, hundreds of whom are feared trapped in the tunnels and underground areas of 12 hydropower projects in Nepal after the devastating flash floods, ​the ⁠country’s disaster ​management authority has said.
The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris on Wednesday last week has risen to 939 people, with 16 more dead reported in Tibet.   More than 4,400 are missing on the two sides of the border.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal rescuers race to reach hundreds feared trapped in hydropower tunnels

articles.author: Cait Kelly in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Majority of missing Australians were near Gyirong Port minutes before impact. Rescuers say the area is now destroyed, covered in metres of silt and debris

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

It has been almost a week since the catastrophic floods in Nepal and not even a vehicle can get into the area where the majority of missing Australians were last heard from.
Gyirong Port, the border area between Nepal and China, was the first to be hit. Images from Chinese rescue teams who have managed to get in by helicopter or hiking show the area has been completely flattened. The immigration building, the power lines, everything, just wiped away.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Border area between Nepal and China where 33 Australians are missing still almost entirely cut off

articles.author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
articles.description:
Berlin expected to outline response to incident this month widely speculated to have been coordinated by Russia
The German government is imminently expected to announce who it believes was behind a suspected drone attack on a Ukrainian cargo plane earlier this month and to outline its response to the incident in coordination with its European and Nato partners.
The chancellor, Friedrich Merz, told the public broadcaster ARD in an interview on Sunday evening: “We are in the process of concluding the investigations; we have reached a broad agreement within the federal government on how we will respond, and we will make this clear in the coming days. It won’t take much longer.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Germany poised to identify suspect in Leipzig drone attack on Ukrainian plane

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Cape Town stunt sparks major debate over safety risks

Airlink insists flyby conducted according to regulations

A pre-game stunt involving two passenger jets flying dramatically low over a stadium in South Africa drew huge cheers from the estimated crowd of 56,000 people, but also sparked a major debate over safety risks. The flyby by two Embraer jets, operated by the local airline Airlink, happened on Saturday before the second rugby union Test between South Africa and New Zealand in Cape Town.
The flight tracking service Flightradar24 estimated that the lead jet passed just 41-46 feet (12-14 metres) above the roof of Cape Town Stadium, with the crowd and the world’s top-ranked rugby teams below. The second jet, which was very close behind, flew through a cloud of pink dust that shot up from the stadium roof as part of the show.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South African airline defends dramatic low-level flyby before rugby union clash

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Trump’s Operation Economic Outcast is expected to push many Iranians into deeper poverty as food inflation soars
For many Iranians, the new US sanctions campaign, called Operation Economic Outcast, seems superfluous given the grim economic situation in their country.
Iranians are facing runaway food inflation, closed petrol stations and a seemingly never-ending depreciation of the nation’s currency caused by a lack of foreign exchange reserves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran’s economy in crisis as US launches new sanctions campaign

articles.author: Reuters in Geneva
articles.description:
Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination
A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination.
Guidance published on Monday by the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (CERD) said the obligations arose from ⁠a legally binding 1965 convention on racial discrimination, not from the legal standards that existed when the slave trade took place.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Countries legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, says UN committee

articles.author: Sam Jones in Madrid
articles.description:
Pedro Sánchez says two countries cooperating and accuses Israel and Russia of spreading fake news about migration
Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has said there is no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta but accused Israel and Russia of spreading disinformation.
As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter the Spanish enclave at the end of July. The influx of about 70,000 men, women and children unleashed a political crisis, a humanitarian emergency and reignited tensions within the EU over immigration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Morocco not to blame for Ceuta border breach, says Spanish PM

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
US attacks Iranian rocket launchers on island in strait of Hormuz and Tehran targets US bases in Jordan and UAE
The US has reverted to military attacks on Iran for the first time in a month, firing missiles and drones at Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz, prompting the Iranian military to attack US military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates.
US Central Command said it acted late on Sunday after it detected the Iranians planning to fire fresh mines into the strait. Last week Donald Trump claimed the US navy had cleared the strait of mines for the first time since the conflict started on 28 February, a claim the Iranians rejected as lies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: First US military attacks on Iran in a month prompt retaliation

articles.author: Danny Vincent in Hong Kong
articles.description:
Rights group claims 300 homes were destroyed in Tibet and number of missing people is ‘far higher’ than Beijing admits
A Tibetan advocacy group says hundreds of homes were destroyed on the Tibetan side of the border in last week’s deadly floods, raising questions about Beijing’s official account of the scale of the disaster.
Public discussion about the flash floods has been restricted, with security officials in Tibet announcing on Sunday that it had penalised at least 10 people for sharing “false disaster information”. There was no further information on the nature of the penalties.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China is concealing scale of flood disaster, say Tibet campaigners

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Organisers say people must revive spiritual relationship with food amid double threat of climate crisis and conflict
Mending the broken food system under the threat of climate-driven weather extremes will require more than economic fixes and intensive agriculture, according to the organisers of a pioneering summit this week, who say the world must revive its spiritual relationship with food.
Delegates from more than 60 countries and the UN will gather for the next five days in Paro in the tiny Himalayan nation of Bhutan for the world’s first “conscious food summit”, which will bring together governments and farmers, mindfulness experts and yoga therapists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bhutan hosts first ‘conscious food summit’ amid threats to global supplies

articles.author: Morgan Thomas for MetDesk
articles.description:
More than 200mm of rain forecast in parts of South Korea, while parts of southern Europe to be 10C above average
South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for heavy rain expected this week, with rainfall totals across central and northern parts of the country forecast to exceed 200mm in some areas.
South Korea was battered by heavy rainfall earlier this month and some areas were particularly hard hit. Over the weekend further thunderstorms pushed into the region and these are expected to cause disruption through Monday. This heavy rain is caused by a series of severe thunderstorms that developed over the Yellow Sea, on the western side of South Korea, and will slowly push eastwards on Monday before easing on Tuesday. These storms have been strengthened by the very warm Yellow Sea, which now has a surface temperature of 29C, 4C above the climatological average.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea

articles.author: Hettie O'Brien
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: As rescuers search for survivors after catastrophic floods, the disaster offers a stark warning about the climate risks facing the region, and the world
Good morning. Over the weekend, rescue workers in Nepal and Tibet raced to find people who are still trapped in villages affected by catastrophic flash floods. As of this morning, the death toll stands at 903, and more than 4,000 people are missing.
For those of you reading this in a place where life continues as usual, the scale of devastation is hard to fathom. In a matter of minutes, a torrent of mud and debris engulfed entire villages, snapped bridges and swept away people’s homes and families. Some survivors are marooned on top of buildings that rescue workers can’t reach. Others are trapped in tunnels beneath t…
articles.title: Monday briefing: Nepal and Tibet’s floods are a warning for the future

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Meanwhile, Trump posts video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America sign
Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA.
Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada erects giant ‘Lake Ontario’ sign as spat with Trump over name escalates

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis and agencies
articles.description:
Total of 804 confirmed dead and more than 3,000 missing amid threat of fresh inundation

‘Their whole village has disappeared’: frantic hunt for survivors in Kathmandu hospital

Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet have battled through leg-sucking mud amid the threat of fresh flooding to search for thousands of people still missing after a deadly wall of water swept through the Himalayan border zone, engulfing entire villages.
The latest updates on Sunday put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There was a total of 804 confirmed deaths across Nepal and Tibet, and reports of some bodies swept downstream possibly as far as India.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal-Tibet deaths from flash flooding rise amid race to free workers in tunnel

articles.author: Harry Cockburn
articles.description:
Rajendra Dawadi ordered students to higher ground with moments to spare after receiving warnings from upstream
A headteacher in Nepal evacuated 900 children from a school moments before a deadly wall of water struck their town amid the devastating flash floods that have killed almost 800 people and left thousands missing.
Rajendra Dawadi decided to halt classes and order children to higher ground after receiving warnings about the scale of the flooding heading their way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Headteacher saves 900 children from deadly flash flood in Nepal

articles.author: Raphael Boyd
articles.description:
Total number of missing Britons between Tibet and Nepal at 48 as Beijing mobilises more than 2,100 rescue workers
Fifteen British nationals are reported to be missing in China as the search continues for survivors of the devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet.
Nepali and Chinese authorities confirmed an updated death toll of at least 810 on Sunday. More than 3,000 people are believed missing after flash floods triggered by a massive glacier collapse in the Himalayas on Wednesday engulfed Gyirong port on the Nepal-China border.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fifteen Britons among 261 foreigners missing in China after floods

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Deal that will reportedly see US take control of 65bn barrels of Venezuelan oil has provoked outrage in her country
Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has defended her government’s highly controversial energy deal with Donald Trump, insisting the South American country will maintain ownership and sovereignty over its massive oil reserves.
Rodríguez, who assumed power in January after Trump ordered the abduction of the president, Nicolás Maduro, took to the airwaves on Saturday to push back against criticism of what the US president has called “the biggest oil deal in world history”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Venezuela’s Delcy Rodríguez defends ‘endless’ benefits of her oil deal with Trump

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
More traumatised civilians are arriving every day at ‘shockingly overcrowded’ El Obeid and camps on its outskirts
Humanitarian conditions in the Sudanese city of El Obeid and two camps on its outskirts are dire and deteriorating, according to people on the ground, as civilians displaced by fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia continue to pour in from the surrounding countryside.
The UN says more than 15,000 families have arrived since mid-July, joining more than 200,000 people who arrived in the first half of the year, according to government figures cited by Save the Children.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: People fleeing Sudan civil war face ‘dire and deteriorating’ conditions in refuge city

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Matt Bradley and crew assaulted while interviewing woman who said settlers had driven family out of home
A Palestinian woman and an NBC News team are reported to have been attacked and injured by masked Israeli settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Saturday, amid worsening confrontations in the area.
Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Palestinian woman and NBC News team reportedly attacked in West Bank

articles.author: Daniela Díaz in Valle del Guamuez and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Fighters in legal limbo after accepting ‘total peace’ plan of Petro government just days before hardliner Abelardo De la Espriella took over
In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine guns and grenade launchers.
They also stripped off their heavy tactical vests, field packs and camouflage uniforms, which were each piled into a bonfire to mark the beginning of a new life away from an armed conflict that has claimed nearly half a million lives in the last six decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?

articles.author: Wendy Frew ; Lucy Campbell, Keely Aouga, Nadeem Badshah, Tom Ambrose, Mabel Banfield-Nwachi, Taz Ali and Adam Fulton
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed

‘The flood took everything I have’: survivors grieve for relatives and homes swept away in Nepal

The army is still working to safely evacuate more than 100 people trapped in the same tunnel.

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
US president says US will have ‘majority’ control of 65bn barrels of proven oil reserves
Donald Trump announced Friday a new US oil agreement with Venezuela’s interim president Delcy Rodríguez, saying the US will have “majority” control of 65bn barrels of proven oil reserves.
The terms of the agreement remain to be seen, but the US president said on his social-media platform that it had been brokered “through a partnership with ⁠private business” by his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, and defense secretary, Pete Hegseth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces new US oil agreement with Venezuela

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Critics call move to gain long-term access to country’s massive energy reserves  ‘predatory’ and ‘unconstitutional’
Reports that the US is preparing to claim a big stake in Venezuela’s massive energy reserves have sparked an outcry, with critics describing the move as “predatory” and a “rapacious” land grab.
Several media outlets this week reported that the Trump administration – which abducted Venezuela’s authoritarian president, Nicolás Maduro, in January and has steered the South American country ever since – hopes to secure long-term access to its oil and gasfields.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Venezuelan opposition up in arms over reports US wants big stake in oil and gas

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Police hunt two suspects after historic 200-carat piece is snatched from Austrian museum during opening hours
Austrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds that was on loan to a museum in Vienna and once belonged to Egyptian royalty.
Authorities in the capital released pictures of the suspects captured by security cameras during the heist at the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK), amid a rash of spectacular smash-and-grab thefts from European cultural institutions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian queen’s 673-diamond necklace stolen in Vienna smash-and-grab raid

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Resignation comes after months of turmoil at Pentagon, from leaked investigation to ousting of senior officials
Army secretary Dan Driscoll has handed his resignation to Donald Trump, the White House said on Monday, becoming the latest high-profile figure to depart the defense department.
The army official, who is second in line to defense secretary Pete Hegseth, had reportedly been eyeing an exit from the Pentagon amid apparent friction with the secretary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US army secretary Dan Driscoll resigns over reported friction with Pete Hegseth

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Justices’ 5-4 ruling permits Trump administration appeal to block lower court order halting above-ground work
A divided US supreme court has permitted Donald Trump to continue building his controversial $400m White House ballroom despite legal challenges, raising the likelihood it will be completed.
In a 5-4 ruling, the justices permitted the Trump administration’s request to ⁠block a lower court order that had halted above-ground construction of the project while a lawsuit by a historic preservation group seeks to block it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US supreme court allows Trump to keep building $400m White House ballroom

articles.author: Shrai Popat and agencies
articles.description:
Letter from chair of joint chiefs of staff addresses concerns over Trump officials using military to interfere with vote
The highest‑ranking US military officer says there are no plans to deploy troops to polling places during the November midterm elections – responding to Senator Elissa Slotkin’s request for information amid concerns about whether the Trump administration might send service members to election sites.
In a letter obtained by the Guardian, first reported by the Associated Press, Gen Dan Caine, chair of the joint chiefs of staff, told Slotkin “the Joint Force has no plans to send Federal military personnel or Federalized members of the National Guard to polling places during the 2026 elections”. He added that there are also “no plans to use such personnel to seize ballots, voting machines, or other election‑related material”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US military has no plans to send troops to midterm polling sites, Dan Caine says

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
RFK Jr, the health secretary, has suggested the deaths were ‘fabricated’ while the CDC claimed it was reviewing them
Top US health officials and government agencies are currently not including the two recent measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania in their counts.
“This is highly unusual,” said Debra Houry, former chief medical officer of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). She noted that this did not happen with the three deaths reported from measles in Texas and New Mexico last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US health officials exclude measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania from counts

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Santos was accused of profiting from bets tied to his attendance at Trump’s State of the Union address
George Santos, the former Republican congressman whose political career collapsed under a mountain of lies, has become the first person ever handed a lifetime ban by the prediction-market platform Kalshi.
The company announced the permanent suspension on Monday, along with a $71,356 fine, after federal regulators accused Santos of profiting from bets tied to his own attendance at Donald Trump’s State of the Union address earlier this year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos from prediction platform for life

articles.author: Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders
articles.description:
The technology can help candidates listen more deeply to voters, as examples from Japan and Scotland show
There are plenty of signs that AI will make all of our experiences of the US midterm elections worse. Voters have anxiety about AI’s impacts on the country. Politicos are using AI deepfakes to spread lies. The White House is posting slopaganda.
Meanwhile, candidates are missing a real opportunity to use AI to make campaigning better. The technology can help candidates listen more deeply to voters’ concerns, engage constituents more inclusively, and formulate policy platforms that are more responsive to our input. There are vanishingly few examples of this in US politics, but groups in Japan, Scotland and the US’s own academic and private institutions show how that could change.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI is hurting US politics. Here’s how candidates could use it for good | Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

articles.author: Aaron Regunberg
articles.description:
The movement against datacenters is uniting Americans because they perfectly illustrate how a few individuals hold all the power to control decisions that affect our lives
Bryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade. The lead organizer with Citizens Action Coalition (CAC), a consumer and environmental organization, he usually encounters a mix of reactions when he’s out canvassing; whatever issue he’s talking about, there’s always at least a few people on the other side. But at a recent festival in the rural town of Monrovia, Indiana, he was struck by an unusual spirit of unity.
He was there about a proposed datacenter, a 550-acre (222-hectare) Google project in this small town of 1,600 people. “I had 50 people I talked to,” Gustafson told me. “Nobody wanted that datacenter in their community. And at least a half a dozen people came up to me to say, ‘Hey, I voted for Trump. What the heck’s he doing, supporting these things?’”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The datacenter backlash is bringing the entire political spectrum together – against big tech billionaires

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Patients are showing up ‘later and sicker’ for abortion care as more US states adopt bans and significant restrictions
Providers are seeing more patients in need of abortions later in pregnancy as abortion bans and restrictions proliferate in US states, all while access to insurance falls.
Those bans and restrictions have also meant that later abortion care access has grown over the past decade in a handful of haven states and cities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘There’s no place to go’: providers see more abortions later in pregnancy as bans spread in US

articles.author: Emma Beddington
articles.description:
US republicans are tarnishing their plant-eating opponents at every opportunity. Yet vegans are perfectly suited to hold power – let me count the ways
Cool news, fellow soy boys and girls – we’ve been promoted from feeble, tofu-eating wokerati to dangerous radicals unfit for public office. Politico reports that US Republicans have started throwing “vegan” around as a tactic to tarnish their political opponents. “He’s a vegan,” Trump warned of Democratic Texas senatorial candidate James Talarico in May, while Talarico’s opponent, state attorney-general Ken Paxton, is trying to get the nickname “Tofu Talarico” to stick. Paxton also called him “a vegan who thinks God is non-binary”, which I find hilarious as a political put-down – give the man a Netflix special. (Sidenote: I investigated, and according to the Catholic catechism, God is “neither man nor woman”.)
Republicans have also been digging up past pro-plant-based statements from Colorado congressional candidate Manny Rutinel: a campaign committee press secretary described him on X as “a far-left vegan activist who wants to end animal agriculture”, posting an old pic of Rutinel bare-chested and wearing a Peta anti-meat banner. Other Dems have also been accused of, erm, liking animals and eating plants: Arizona congressional candidate Amish Shah has been attacked for his “wacky liberal agenda pushing vegan policies” and Lindsay James in Iowa drew heat for merely supporting the idea of “meatless May”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is 'vegan' suddenly being used as a slur? | Emma Beddington

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Angie Nixon won one of the biggest upsets in US midterm primaries – and if elected, the Democrat would be the first African American senator in Florida history
The Democratic establishment had the money, the machinery and the candidate with national name recognition. Angie Nixon had a bookshop called Café Resistance and a grassroots campaign for the Senate. On primary election night in Florida, Nixon won in arguably the biggest upset of the primary season. But at least one person was not shocked: Angie Nixon herself. “We weren’t surprised,” the 42-year-old reflects after overcoming a vast fundraising disadvantage to defeat Alex Vindman, a combat veteran who testified against Donald Trump during his first impeachment. “We actually knew we were going to win; we just didn’t know that we were going to win by that much. We put in the work and so super excited about the outcome. It shows that good old-fashioned grassroots organising will beat big money each and every day.”
Nixon won 56.1% of the vote to Vindman’s 43.9%. The result stirred tensions within the Democratic party in a year defined by the struggle between moderates and economic populists. In Florida – a state that has trended increasingly Republican in recent years and is now Trump’s home state – Democrats have now nominated a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) who speaks openly about class war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Grassroots will beat big money every day’: can a DSA member flip a Republican Senate seat?

articles.author: Sina Toossi
articles.description:
As with its approach to Hormuz, the US has mistaken applying pressure for an actual strategy. But Tehran has chips of its own to play
Donald Trump has found a new way to promise victory over Iran. After months of war have failed to force Iran’s capitulation or collapse, his administration has unveiled what the US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, calls Operation Economic Outcast: an effort to cut it off from what remains of the global economy and threaten foreign governments, banks and companies with sanctions if they continue doing business with Tehran.
There is no question that Iran is vulnerable. Its economy has been battered by years of sanctions, war and a months-long US naval blockade. Iranian officials acknowledge that oil exports and access to foreign currency have been severely constrained. Ordinary Iranians are already enduring high inflation, currency depreciation and worsening living standards. Further economic strangulation will inflict significant additional hardship.
Sina Toossi is a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, where his work focuses on US-Iran relations, US policy toward the Middle East and nuclear issues
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s ‘economic D-day’ against Iran risks driving the stakes even higher | Sina Toossi

articles.author: George Chidi in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina
articles.description:
In deep red South Carolina, the president helped stoke apprehension of a deeper red surge ahead of November’s US midterm elections
After casting his vote in South Carolina, a man who introduced himself as Chestnut was unwilling to give his full name. “You don’t have a need to know,” the air force veteran declared. He was, however, happy to share his views.
“I’m a true American. I believe in the USA,” said the man, outside Christ the Servant Lutheran church in Conway. “And I don’t believe in communism or socialism.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Donald Trump’s bid to brand Democrats as ‘radical’ communists working?

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Ignore Iran, the Epstein files, and your wallet – not to mention Trump’s plummeting approval ratings
Don’t mention the war! Or the economy, for that matter. Or the Epstein files. Or Natalie Harp. Or “affordability”, which, as Donald Trump recently said at a rally, is a word that was “never used” by the media before he took office. Best not to talk about anything that affects ordinary people or embarrasses the president, really. Instead, let’s all rejoice in Trump’s latest triumph: renaming Lake Ontario, which is shared by Canada and the US, as Lake America.
On Thursday, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to America-fy the lake’s name on US maps and documents, which is an excellent use of time and resources. I suppose we can at least be thankful that the president, who is trying to slap his own name on everything from airports to the Kennedy Center, didn’t decree that the body of water be called Lake Trump.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The rebranding of ‘Lake America’ is Trump’s desperate attempt to distract us | Arwa Mahdawi

Jonathan Freedland speaks to Dan Alexander of Forbes about how Donald Trump made so much money last year at the same time trade wars, military wars and a rising national debt hurt the US economy

One of Donald Trump’s closest and most devoted aides, Natalie Harp, has faced intense media scrutiny this week, after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, name-checked her in a speech that went viral. So what do we know about Harp, who is often referred to as the ‘human printer’? And why is everybody talking about her relationship with Trump? Helen Pidd speaks to international news editor Paul Owen

articles.description:
Less than three months to go until the midterms, voters are thinking about grocery prices, the Iran war and… datacentres.

This week, Jonathan Freedland speaks to historian Jill Lepore about how this latest AI backlash could influence those all-important elections in November. Are we seeing the beginning of the end of the 'artificial state'?

articles.title: Historian Jill Lepore on the datacentre backlash | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Jane Clinton and Majidah Chowdhury
articles.description:
While many young people have found jobs and built careers, some have struggled to complete their courses

The crisis in the youth employment market, with almost a million young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) across the UK, has placed fresh emphasis on ways of getting employees into the workforce.
The government hopes to increase focus on technical and vocational learning in England from the age of 14. In parallel, there is an ambition to create thousands more apprenticeships.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A huge learning curve’: apprentices on the benefits and pitfalls of vocational training

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Chancellor says he wants everyone from apprentices to senior economists to take part in brainstorming exercise
John Healey has asked junior Treasury staff – including IT workers and apprentices – to send him ideas for his October budget, saying he will listen to all suggestions regardless of grade or profession.
The chancellor’s unorthodox approach comes as he faces a tricky autumn with expected inflation rises, sluggish growth and potential cuts from other departments to fund extra defence spending.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: John Healey invites October budget ideas from Treasury staff of all levels

articles.author: Hilary Osborne
articles.description:
Exclusive: FCA pressures firms to do more to sort 760,000 accounts as watchdog urges families to use free tracking service
Child trust fund providers are being put under the spotlight to check they are treating savers fairly and doing all they can to reunite young people with lost accounts.
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said about 760,000 accounts worth an average of £2,000 were yet to be claimed – more than £1.5bn in total – as it launched a review of the market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Child trust fund firms face review over efforts to find who owns £1.5bn worth of pots

articles.author: Damien Gayle Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Report calls for legally binding targets to cut microplastic pollution as soil ‘is a complex living ecosystem’
The accumulation of microplastics in soil presents an emerging threat to the UK’s food security, according to scientists, MPs and campaigners who have called for legally binding targets to cut microplastic pollution.
UK agricultural soils have been identified as among the most contaminated by microplastics in Europe, often as a result of repeated applications of sludge from water treatment works as fertiliser, according to a report published by the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) on microplastics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rising microplastics in soil a threat to UK food security, MPs and campaigners say

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Premium of nearly 10% paid by housebuyers comparable with cost of a cheaper private school over seven years
A house near a top state secondary school costs an extra £40,000 on average, according to research that reveals education premiums that rank alongside some private school fees.
The average property in a postcode district that includes a top 50 state secondary commands a price tag of £415,791, compared with £375,217 across the wider local authority areas in which those schools are located, a UK-wide analysis by the estate agent Yopa found.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK houses near top state secondary schools cost £40,000 more, research reveals

articles.author: Helena Horton and Harry Cockburn
articles.description:
From a darling of the Tory right to a moderate former army officer, we profile the key players

Andrew Griffith and Tom Tugendhat join Badenoch’s top team in Tory reshuffle

Kemi Badenoch has kicked off the return to parliament with a reshuffle of her top team in order to take on Andy Burnham and Reform UK. She has made sweeping changes to the shadow cabinet and ruthlessly axed her shadow chancellor. Here is a run-down of the new characters sitting across from Labour on the opposition frontbench.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team?

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Prime minister wants to ‘bring back hope’ by tackling cost of living as MPs call for electoral reform
Andy Burnham will drive home his pledge to bring more essential services back into public control, telling MPs in the Commons on Tuesday that it will be the only way to improve growth across the country.
Burnham will address the house for the first time in 16 years from the frontbench, and six weeks since he became prime minister, after spending the summer recess announcing a slew of policies that will now be put before MPs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More public control is the way to grow UK economy, Burnham to tell MPs

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Conservative leader sacks shadow chancellor Mel Stride and shadow foreign secretary Priti Patel

Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team?

Kemi Badenoch sacked her shadow chancellor, Mel Stride, and the shadow foreign secretary, Priti Patel, in a sweeping Conservative reshuffle on Monday, replacing Stride with Andrew Griffith, and Patel with Tom Tugendhat.
Stride, who had been shadow chancellor since Badenoch became leader, was widely seen among Tories as failing to make an impression at a time when Labour had been under pressure over the economy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andrew Griffith and Tom Tugendhat join Badenoch’s top team in Tory reshuffle

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Body of victim thought to be in her 70s found in bin bag in walled garden area of Stanley Park on Friday
Police in Liverpool have urged members of the public to come forward with information after the body of an unknown woman believed to be in her 70s was found in a black bin bag in a popular park.
Merseyside police were contacted by a passerby who had found the woman’s body in Stanley Park, in the Anfield area of Liverpool, at about 5.25pm on Friday 28 August.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police appeal after unidentified woman’s body found in Liverpool park

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor in Munich
articles.description:
Technology trained on millions of routine ECGs could fast-track high-risk patients for treatment
Doctors have developed a “superhuman” AI tool that can spot heart disease in less than two seconds.
The groundbreaking technology has been trained on millions of patients and works by extracting more information from a routine electrocardiogram (ECG) than the human eye can typically see.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Superhuman’ AI tool spots heart disease in less than 2 seconds

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Labour leader faces tough decisions on issues such as North Sea drilling, electoral reform and defence spending

After a relatively cheery summer in which he announced a range of eye-catching cost of living policies, Andy Burnham may find his return to parliament this week to be a rude awakening.
While the new prime minister has enjoyed some success in the polls, he is faced with many of the same problems that stymied Keir Starmer and has some difficult and unpopular choices to make.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham’s bumpy ride ahead: PM’s in-tray full of dilemmas as parliament returns

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Telecoms company to benefit from soaring prices for recycled metal recovered from full-fibre broadband rollout
BT is on track for an estimated £2bn-plus windfall over the next decade from selling off old copper cabling, as it cashes in on soaring prices amid the AI market frenzy and switches the UK’s network to full-fibre broadband.
Copper is one of the main beneficiaries of the “electrification of everything”, essential for the rapid growth of AI datacentres, electronics and the fast-growing renewable energy industry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BT on track for estimated £2bn windfall from selling old copper amid AI boom

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Dr Will Tullett says better understanding of scents can improve wellbeing and perception of the world
Children need a better education in sniffing aromas, a leading historian of smells has said, noting it may improve their wellbeing and help them understand the world around them.
Dr Will Tullett, of the University of York, said pollution had been found to impair people’s olfactory abilities, while many objects and substances today – from margarines to car interiors and even our own homes – were stripped of their original smells and “reodourised” with synthetic scents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Smelling test: children need education in sniffing aromas, scientist says

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Exclusive: Labour MPs believe Gordon Brown-era SMC has become ineffective and its work ‘should be a core function of government’
Ministers are considering a shake-up of the government’s social mobility watchdog that could range from giving it more teeth to abolishing it outright.
The move comes amid concerns that the Social Mobility Commission (SMC) – originally conceived under Gordon Brown’s government in 2010 – has become ineffective.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK social mobility watchdog could be axed as ministers plan shake-up

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political corresponent
articles.description:
Clacton, funding, internal divisions – party prepares for annual conference next week after a season of missteps
Senior Reform UK figures like to boast that the summer time – and parliament’s longest recess – is when the party makes hay.
Supposedly, it is when Nigel Farage and co can muscle in on the news cycle with provocative statements and new policies, painting “establishment” opponents as workshy layabouts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Reform UK recover from its summer horribilis?

articles.author: Nick Sommerlad
articles.description:
Exclusive: How a court case over an unoccupied office block could end a widely used tax avoidance scheme
From the outside, the seven-storey building at 2 America Square looks like any other office block in the heart of London’s financial district.
Located about half a mile from Tower Bridge, one might expect it to be a hive of commercial activity, teeming with employees holding important meetings. However, much of the property is home not to staff vying for their next bonus, but to stacks of nondescript black boxes arranged in neat lines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The London office, the empty boxes and the £1bn tax loophole

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Andy Burnham urged to seek consensus over response to extreme heat and forthcoming ‘super El Niño’
Andy Burnham should call a cross-party meeting to discuss the UK’s response to worsening extreme weather, including the forthcoming ‘super El Niño’, the Liberal Democrats have said.
The prime minister chaired a Cobra emergency meeting on the drought earlier this month but there has been little from the government on the wider threats posed by five successive heatwaves since May and expected global issues with food shortages and inflation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cross-party talks needed to tackle climate crisis, say Lib Dems

articles.author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
articles.description:
Concern among staff that fragile artwork’s scarce ‘light hours’ given to someone with no known interest in museum
The British Museum privately hosted the Donald Trump-supporting tech billionaire Peter Thiel in the exhibition space of the Bayeux tapestry earlier this month, the Guardian understands.
The museum’s director of development, Charlotte Appleyard, hosted the PayPal founder at a VIP viewing of the tapestry, which is yet to open to the public, on 18 August.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Museum hosted Palantir founder Peter Thiel in private viewing of Bayeux tapestry

articles.author: Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Despite plans to scrap the lifetime Isa, experts still advise you open one now and not wait for the new first-time buyer account to launch
If you want to start saving towards your first home, don’t wait until a new Isa just for first-time buyers goes on sale. That is the advice from experts after more details emerged about a savings account the government plans to launch to help people get a foot on the property ladder.
The first-time buyer Isa is likely to replace the existing lifetime Isa in two years and is supposed to be simpler than the older account. However, it looks as if the financial benefits won’t be as attractive as those offered by the current product, so there’s no advantage in hanging around.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: First-time buyer Isa v lifetime Isa – which one should you choose?

articles.author: Simon Goodley
articles.description:
Nationwide research also shows average 14% premium for housing in national landscapes of England and Wales
Housebuyers are paying a premium of almost a quarter to own a property located within a UK national park, with the New Forest the most expensive national park to live in, according to Britain’s biggest building society.
Nationwide found that a property located within a national park cost 24% more on average than a similar property elsewhere, while buyers were also stumping up a 6% premium for homes within three miles of a national park.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Properties in UK national parks command 24% premium, study finds

articles.author: Presented by Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker, produced by Maz Ebtehaj and Ned Carter Miles, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Frankie Tobi
articles.description:
Will the UK ever rejoin the EU? Who is funding Andy Burnham? And will the bedroom tax be scrapped? In a special episode, Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker answer some of your questions
